_comment: Argmax-vs-sampled self-play campaign, built on the v0.14.0 config (history=16, eta=0.5, lr=5e-5, 6x128 resnet, 80k steps) -- the eta=0.5 seed-0 run that tied for best on the pooled Elo ladder. Run with: uv run python scripts/train_campaign.py --sweep sweep_argmax.json [--dry-run]. The single axis is train.selfplay_sample: true = sample the masked softmax (the DeepNash/R-NaD default), false = argmax (greedy) action selection during self-play. 6 runs = 3 seeds (0,1,2) x 2 modes, so the mode effect can be read against seed noise -- essential here, because the existing leaderboard showed ~140 Elo spread across four identical-config seeds, i.e. a 2-run comparison would be uninterpretable. train.eval_sample is pinned false (greedy) for EVERY run so evaluation is identical regardless of how the run was trained; only the training-time behavior differs. WARNING on the argmax arm: greedy self-play makes trajectories deterministic for a fixed network, which collapses exploration and breaks R-NaD's on-policy assumption (the behavior policy mu is no longer the softmax the importance ratios in v-trace assume, so rho/c are computed against a distribution the actor never actually sampled from). These runs are expected to be WEAKER and possibly degenerate; the point is to measure and document that, not to find a better agent.

runs._comment: Control arm, seed 0: stochastic self-play (masked-softmax sampling), the canonical R-NaD behavior and an as-close-as-possible re-run of v0.14.0. Anchors the comparison and re-measures seed noise on the current code.
runs.name: argmax-sampled-seed-0

runs._comment: Treatment arm, seed 0: greedy (argmax) self-play. Deterministic action selection for a fixed network -- exploration comes only from weight updates and color/opening asymmetry, not from the policy itself.
runs.name: argmax-greedy-seed-0
